content.user_title: Review Code for Security and Quality
content.value_statement: Manual code reviews can miss security, performance, and testing issues. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured review workflow with checklists and helper scan guidance.
actual_capabilities: Guides reviews across security, code quality, performance, testing, and documentation.
Provides checklists for common vulnerability patterns such as injection, XSS, secrets, and weak cryptography.
Documents optional commands for Bandit, Safety, ESLint, gosec, Radon, and Pylint.
Includes a Python helper script that can run Bandit, Radon, Pylint, and Safety when installed.
Generates Markdown, text, or JSON-style review reports from helper scan results.
Offers language-specific review prompts for Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Java, and Go.
limitations: The helper script depends on external tools that may not be installed locally.
Automated scan results still require human validation before action.
The security examples are educational and are not a replacement for dedicated threat modeling.
The helper script focuses mainly on Python tooling and general checklist guidance.

use_cases.title: Review a Pull Request
use_cases.description: Check a feature or bug fix for security, maintainability, tests, and documentation before merge.

use_cases.title: Audit a Codebase Before Release
use_cases.description: Run structured checks for vulnerabilities, dependency issues, complexity, and missing tests before deployment.

use_cases.title: Teach Review Standards
use_cases.description: Use the checklists and examples to train reviewers on common risks and consistent feedback.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Pull Request Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a small change
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this change for correctness, security issues, missing tests, and documentation gaps. Prioritize findings that could affect users.

prompt_templates.title: Security-Focused Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Review code that touches authentication, data access, or user input
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a security-focused review of this code. Check input validation, authorization, secrets handling, injection risks, and unsafe deserialization.

prompt_templates.title: Performance and Maintainability Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Review a larger refactor or backend change
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this change for performance bottlenecks, unnecessary complexity, resource leaks, and maintainability issues. Separate critical risks from cleanup suggestions.

prompt_templates.title: Release Readiness Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this code for release readiness. Cover security, correctness, performance, observability, test coverage, rollback concerns, and documentation requirements.

output_examples.input: Review a pull request that adds a new API endpoint.
output: Security: verify authentication and authorization on the endpoint.
Correctness: check request validation and error handling.
Testing: add negative tests for invalid input and forbidden access.

output_examples.input: Run a security-focused review of a Python service.
output: High priority: check for SQL injection and unsafe file access.
Medium priority: verify secrets are not logged.
Follow-up: run Bandit and dependency checks if the tools are installed.

output_examples.input: Review a performance-sensitive data processing change.
output: Performance: inspect nested loops and repeated database calls.
Testing: add coverage for large input sizes and timeout behavior.

best_practices: Start with the change context and user impact before listing issues.
Prioritize security and correctness findings over style feedback.
Validate automated tool output before treating it as a blocking issue.
anti_patterns: Do not treat checklist completion as proof that the code is safe.
Do not run helper scans on untrusted code without understanding local execution risk.
Do not mix critical findings with minor style comments in the same priority level.

faq.question: Does this skill automatically fix code?
faq.answer: No. It guides review and can generate reports, but fixes require separate implementation work.

faq.question: Can it run security tools?
faq.answer: The included helper script can call tools such as Bandit, Radon, Pylint, and Safety if they are installed.

faq.question: Is it only for Python projects?
faq.answer: No. The guidance covers several languages, but the helper script is strongest for Python analysis.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is suitable for Claude Code workflows that review local diffs or repository files.

faq.question: Does it replace human review?
faq.answer: No. It helps structure review and surface risks, but human judgment is still required.

faq.question: What should I do with scan findings?
faq.answer: Confirm each finding in context, prioritize user-impacting issues, and request targeted fixes for real risks.
